title: Compact support and coefficient extension retain the finite-Tor domain
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $h:U\to V$ be a separated finite-type map of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$ in the same class [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$. Use the ordinary constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ for site pullback [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $E_B=E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ for coefficient extension on either site [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor] [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $L\in D^b(U_{\rm et},A)$ have constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, meaning a uniform finite cohomology interval for its tensor with each degree-zero module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf] [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_R^{\rm et}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm et}j_{!,R}^{\rm et}$ and $F_R^{\rm pro}=Rr_{*,R}^{\rm pro}j_{!,R}^{\rm pro}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support] [det-sp-reduction-direct-image]. Then $F_A^{\rm et}L$ and $F_B^{\rm et}(L_B)$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude, and so are their site pullbacks, with intrinsically constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude on the pro-etale site [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. The complexes $(F_A^{\rm et}L)_B$ and $L_B$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude as well. The specified map $N_VF_R^{\rm et}E\to F_R^{\rm pro}N_UE$ obtained by the proper counit mate and the open comparison is an isomorphism for every bounded-below etale input $E$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Consequently all these inputs and actual scalar extensions lie in $D^+$; no finite projective dimension of $B/A$ is assumed. Schemes and Noetherian rings use [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

source.place: Tag 0GL6 (remark-Rf-lower-shriek-change-of-rings), finite-Tor domains for coefficient and composite inputs. Agent reflection argument from the named comparison theorems.

proof.text: Check the comparison and compactification hypotheses. A finite ring is Noetherian: every ideal is generated by its finitely many elements. Each of $U,W,V$ is qcqs: its structure morphism to the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by separatedness; apply qcqs permanence and affine qcqs. Since $U$ is quasi-compact and $W$ quasi-separated, $j$ is quasi-compact. The same permanence lemma makes $r$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. These observations apply to both $R=A,B$, including the zero ring and empty schemes.

For $R=A$ or $B$ and any $E\in D^+(U_{\rm et},R)$, etale $j_!$ is exact, hence $j_!E\in D^+(W_{\rm et},R)$. Right-derived direct image has no cohomology below the lower bound of its input, so $F_R^{\rm et}E\in D^+$. Apply the canonical-mate comparison to $r$ and $j_!E$ and then the open comparison:
$$N_VRr_*^{\rm et}j_!^{\rm et}E\xrightarrow{b_{r,j_!E}}Rr_*^{\rm pro}N_Wj_!^{\rm et}E\xrightarrow{Rr_*^{\rm pro}(\gamma_j)}Rr_*^{\rm pro}j_!^{\rm pro}N_UE.$$
The sheaf comparison $\gamma_j$ extends degreewise to complexes because both open-extension functors and comparison pullback are exact. Its inverse also extends degreewise. Thus both displayed arrows are isomorphisms. This is exactly the specified map: the first arrow is the named counit mate $b$, with its stated counit normalization, and the second is the canonical open comparison; no alternative isomorphism is substituted.

source.place: Canonical counit-mate comparison, composed with open extension comparison; Stacks 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor) and 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing).

proof.text: Now let $E\in D^b_c(U_{\rm et},R)$ have finite Tor amplitude. The Noetherian-coefficient finite-Tor comparison gives $N_UE\in D^b_{ctf}(U_{\rm proet},R)$, with intrinsically constructible cohomology. The single-compactification theorem applies to the given $j,r$ and carries this object to $F_R^{\rm pro}N_UE\in D^b_{ctf}(V_{\rm proet},R)$. Use the finite discrete module-object/ordinary-module equivalence here: it preserves the intrinsic constructible and Tor predicates and identifies the compactification composite with the actual ordinary $Rr_*j_!$ for this same compactification. By Step 2, $N_VF_R^{\rm et}E$ therefore has these properties as well.

source.place: Finite coefficients, chosen compactification, preservation of Dctf; Noetherian finite-Tor comparison.

proof.text: Write $C=F_R^{\rm et}E$. Exactness of $N_V$ gives $H^q(N_VC)\simeq N_VH^q(C)$. The heart comparison is fully faithful, hence detects zero objects: if $N_VM=0$, faithfulness sends $\mathrm{id}_M$ to zero only when $\mathrm{id}_M=0$. Thus the finite cohomology interval of $N_VC$ is also one for $C$. For each $q$, constructible comparison supplies a constructible etale sheaf $M_q$ whose image is $H^q(N_VC)$. Full faithfulness lifts the isomorphism $N_VM_q\simeq N_VH^q(C)$ and its inverse, yielding $M_q\simeq H^q(C)$. Hence $C\in D^b_c$. Only now apply the Noetherian finite-Tor comparison to $C$: any Tor interval for $N_VC$ is a Tor interval for $C$. This proves compact-support preservation for either coefficient ring without assuming constructibility of $C$ beforehand.

source.place: Tag 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible), exact fully faithful comparison, and blueprint Noetherian finite-Tor comparison; explicit reflection argument.

proof.text:
For $T=U$ or $V$ and any bounded constructible finite-Tor etale $A$-complex $K$, form its actual etale scalar extension $K_B$ by K-flat change of rings. Comparison pullback is exact and preserves K-flat models with flat terms. Applying the derived tensor-pullback comparison with the constant factor $B_T$ therefore gives
$$N_T(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\simeq (N_TK)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B.$$
This is an isomorphism of $B$-complexes: on the tensor representatives its map sends $x\otimes b$ to the corresponding pulled-back tensor, and multiplication on the displayed right factor is the $B$-action on both sides. No resolution of $B$ of finite length is used. The Noetherian comparison puts $N_TK$ in the pro-etale finite-Tor constructible domain; clause (2) of the scalar-extension theorem then makes the right-hand side bounded intrinsically constructible with the same Tor interval as $N_TK$.

The reflection argument for these actual scalar extensions does not presuppose that $K_B$ is bounded below. Indeed the exact derived comparison is defined on the unbounded categories and gives $H^q(N_TK_B)\simeq N_TH^q(K_B)$. Faithfulness detects the zero cohomology sheaves outside the finite interval obtained in Step 5. The constructible sheaf equivalence and full faithfulness then show that every $H^q(K_B)$ is constructible, exactly by lifting the isomorphism and its inverse as in Step 4. Therefore $K_B$ is bounded constructible. Applying the Noetherian finite-Tor comparison at this point proves finite Tor amplitude of $K_B$ over $B$. This also establishes its $D^+$ membership before any bounded-below direct-image comparison is applied to it.

source.place: Tag 09AK (lemma-compare-constructible); unbounded exact comparison and explicit cohomology reflection, followed by Noetherian finite-Tor comparison.

proof.text: Instantiate Steps 3–4 with $R=A,E=L$ to obtain $F_A^{\rm et}L$ and its site pullback in the asserted domains. Instantiate Steps 5–6 first with $T=U,K=L$, and then with $T=V,K=F_A^{\rm et}L$: these give the actual $L_B$ and $(F_A^{\rm et}L)_B$ and their site pullbacks. Finally instantiate Steps 3–4 with $R=B,E=L_B$, whose bounded constructible finite-Tor hypotheses were just proved, to obtain $F_B^{\rm et}(L_B)$ and its site pullback. Step 2 applies to every bounded-below input independently of these finiteness assertions. Every complex just listed is bounded and hence belongs to $D^+$; the stated pro-etale compact-support outputs also do, by that comparison. All coefficient hypotheses used were finiteness and primary torsion, never finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$.

The statement matches the pre-delivery copy except for one added citation, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, which types the étale scalar extension; nothing in the mathematics changed. Step 1: qcqs of U, W, V and of j and r follows from finite type, separatedness and permanence, and finite rings are Noetherian. Step 2: the canonical-mate hypotheses hold (Λ finite, r qcqs, j_!E in D^+), and the open comparison extends to complexes degreewise because j_! and ν^* are exact; this gives the specified map. Step 3: Noetherian finite-Tor comparison, then det-sf-comp-coherence-single (any field of characteristic p, j quasi-compact, r proper), bridged to ordinary sheaves by the module-object equivalence for the same compactification. Steps 4 and 6: cohomology is reflected through the exact, fully faithful ν^* and sk-thm-pe-constructible-comparison before the finite-Tor comparison is applied, so the order of hypotheses is correct, and the unbounded exact-functor node avoids assuming K_B is bounded below. Step 5: derived tensor pullback with G=B_T plus clause (2) of the scalar-extension node; no finite projective dimension is used. Step 7: assembly; every clause is covered. Small cases checked: U empty, B=0, F_l[e]/e^2 to F_l with L=A. prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility covers only A_{E,n} and has no Tor clause, so it is not a duplicate. review_split PASS; tool_uses accepted as generic.
